name: High-school AP courses and grade levels
description: Fires on tokens like senior, junior, highschool, AP English and course listings, plus mentions of school year, prom, and not owning a car.

name: First-person accounts of school and learning
description: Fires on first-person contractions (I'm, I've, don't) in long personal narratives about classes, writing assignments, learning skills, and friends.

name: School-related and YouTube channel references
description: Fires on the token school (and variants like scho, scholes) together with mentions of YouTube channels and life.

name: Legal age limits for alcohol, tobacco, consent
description: Fires on legal, age, consent, alcohol, beer, older near statements about minimum ages for drinking, smoking, tattoos, M-rated games, and age of consent.

name: Reflective remarks on life, conflict, and entertainment
description: Fires on life, playing, video game alongside reflective passages about violent conflict as entertainment and on questions about trauma and mental health.

name: Emergency, crisis, and management vocabulary
description: Fires on emergency, crisis, averted, management near references to emergency services and graduating to work in an emergency field.

name: Concessive 'given' clauses
description: Fires on the word given used to introduce a concession or qualifier, as in 'given the length' or 'given that there is past precedent'.

name: Sarcastic argumentative second-person rebuttals
description: Fires on maybe, you're, making fun in long second-person rebuttals that mock an interlocutor's assumptions and personal bubble.

name: Directional phrase 'towards the end'
description: Fires strongly on the preposition towards, especially in the recurring phrase 'towards the end' and similar directional or trajectory expressions.

name: mixed or low-signal feature
description: Top words (happened, poor, poisoned, head, shoulders, bill) and examples span unrelated topics with no coherent shared linguistic theme.
